title: Spotify will now tell you when an artist isn’t real
body: That new singer in your Spotify playlist may have a name, a face, and a carefully written bio. Soon, Spotify may also tell you the person they describe doesn t exist. Beginning in mid-September, the streaming platform will place an "AI Persona" badge on profiles built around AI-generated identities. Music from those profiles will also be excluded from Spotify s editorial playlists and algorithmic recommendations by default, the company announced Aug. 11. Spotify will stop introducing listeners to AI Personas by default. Their songs should no longer pop up in Discover Weekly, Release Radar, or another personalized playlist unless you have already shown interest in the artist. You can still search for, play, and follow them, and following one may tell Spotify that you re open to hearing more. Put simply, the company doesn t want an AI Persona to be something you discover by accident. Credit: Spotify That is also the frustration Spotify says it has heard from listeners, who "don t like seeing an artist profile that seems human, only to find out that the persona is AI-generated," according to the announcement. The data suggest plenty of listeners share that concern. As Mashable reported in 2025 , 97 percent of respondents could not distinguish a fully AI-generated song from one made by humans. Still, 80 percent wanted AI music clearly labeled, and 72 percent wanted to know if a streaming service was recommending it. title: Less than 2.5% of Taylor Farms' recalled lettuce went to Taco Bells
author: Beth Mole
body: Though shredded iceberg lettuce at Taco Bell restaurants has been a prime suspect in an explosive outbreak of the diarrheal parasite Cyclospora , a new report from the Food and Drug Administration finally reveals where all the contaminated lettuce was sold—and only a tiny sliver of it went to Taco Bell locations. The feces-tainted lettuce was sourced from Mexico and sold by Taylor Farms, a mammoth produce provider based in California. Taylor Farms has drawn scrutiny for its ties to the Trump administration and reluctance to provide information amid the outbreak, which has now sickened over 23,000 people across 47 states, killing two and sending over 500 others to the hospital. Taylor Farms reportedly attempted to delay issuing a recall amid the illnesses and, since then, has refused to clearly report how much tainted lettuce it recalled and where all of it had been shipped. The FDA's Enforcement Report finally provides some answers: Taylor Farms recalled a total of 236,192 cases of lettuce due to potential Cyclospora contamination. Of those, only 5,900—just shy of 2.5 percent—were sold to Yum, the parent company of Taco Bell, Pizza Hut, and KFC. The other 97.5 percent of the lettuce that potentially sickened Americans was distributed elsewhere. Read full article Comments

title: Tracking extreme heat by the hour makes climate change seem even worse
author: Scott K. Johnson
body: Global warming is leading to more extremely hot weather. There is perhaps no more obvious consequence of climate change. But changing how we analyze this problem can still help scientists think about it in a different way that may yield surprises. Generally, studies on heat extremes work with some combination of daily minimum, maximum, and mean temperatures. Sometimes they focus on multi-day heatwaves using those metrics, since the discomfort and health impacts increase for longer events. There are different thresholds you can use to define extreme heat in these analyses, either based on past statistics or on the human body’s physiological limits. A new study led by Weilin Liao and Xuanzong Zhang at Sun Yat-sen University tried breaking down heat extremes to the hourly level instead, which reveals some interesting nuances. title: A Google insider spills the tea on how the company forsook its founding ideals
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: In 2018, 20,000 Google employees worldwide made headlines when they staged a walkout to protest how the company had handled sexual misconduct allegations against key corporate executives, among other grievances. One of the organizers was Claire Stapleton , a communications specialist whose distinctive voice and ability to channel the corporate ethos had once earned her the internal moniker "Bard of Google." Six months later, a disillusioned Stapleton resigned, claiming she had been demoted during the most recent restructuring as retaliation for helping to spearhead the walkout. The story of how she went from enthusiastic cheerleader to proactive dissident, and the many lessons she learned along the way, are featured in her new book, Don't Be Evil: Bad Bosses, Fake Promises, and My Escape from Big Tech—A Biting Memoir of Twelve Years Inside Google . Stapleton didn't set out to be a rabble-rouser. When she joined Google out of college in 2007, it was like "getting the golden ticket in Willy Wonka ," she told Ars. Awareness of her good fortune offset any initial uneasiness or skepticism, although Stapleton was sufficiently independent-minded not to move into what was then Google's new corporate housing development in Mountain View, California. Stapleton was very good at her job, and she quickly moved up the ranks, playing a key role in shaping the company's public image. Read full article Comments

author: Jon Brodkin
body: The Federal Communications Commission has been shorthanded throughout President Trump's second term, but it's about to get a new commissioner. Unsurprisingly, Trump is breaking a historical norm with a nomination that would give Republicans a 3-1 advantage on the FCC. Historically, the president and Senate worked together to ensure that the president's party maintained only a one-vote majority. Normally, the president's party has three FCC members while the minority party has two. Instead of the typical 3-2 split, the FCC has operated with a 2-1 Republican majority during Trump's second term. On Friday, Trump nominated Republican Danielle Thumann Severs to take one of the empty spots. Thumann Severs, a lawyer, has been working as FCC Chairman Brendan Carr's senior counsel. title: Gentle Monster trailer sees Léa Seydoux facing dark home truths
body: Something's very off in the trailer for Gentle Monster , with L a Seydoux starring as a woman facing dark truths in her own home. And though the film's absolutely not about the Korean eyewear brand , the director was inspired by the company's name . Written and directed by Marie Kreutzer, the film follows concert pianist Lucy (Seydoux) whose idyllic home life with her husband Philip (Laurence Rupp) and son is shattered when the police show up with a search warrant, accusing Phillip of a heinous crime. Forced to reckon with the accusations against the person she loves, Lucy has more than one lie to untangle, and her son to protect. It's a complicated film, thematically, for Kreutzer, whose 2022 film Corsage starred actor Florian Teichtmeister, who was charged for similar crimes. The director told The Hollywood Reporter in May 2026, "In the middle of that whole scandal and shit storm, I thought maybe I cannot make Gentle Monster anymore, because everyone will always make that connection. It didn t take me very long until to realize that I might have to make it even more." From the trailer, we get a glimpse of director of photography Judith Kaufmann's cinematography, music by Camille, and a powerful performance from Seydoux, who stars alongside Jella Haase and Catherine Deneuve. Gentle Monster will premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF) in September, before its release in select cinemas Oct. 30. The film will then be streaming on Netflix from Nov. 18. title: Claude to start watermarking AI-generated content
body: Anthropic's Claude will start watermarking AI-generated content in compliance with EU rules, the company announced on Tuesday. In a Claude support document, Anthropic wrote that it has signed the EU AI Act's Article 50(2) Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content , and explains how it plans to put those rules into practice. SEE ALSO: Claude Code s auto mode will be on by default, Anthropic confirms Models launched in the EU on or after Aug. 2, 2026, wrote Anthropic, will support watermarking at launch. This includes output from all models including Claude Platform (API), Claude, Claude Code, Claude Cowork, and Claude Tag. Generated text will have embedded watermarks, while generated files will include "digitally signed provenance metadata where supported." Notably, it won't apply only to Europe; instead, the watermarks will appear wherever Claude is offered, worldwide, though Anthropic warns that some platforms or features may not support certain watermarking types. Featured Video For You Is ChatGPT Changing the Way We Write? The watermarks won't be visible if you don't know what you're looking for. For text files, the watermark will be "part of the text" and it will "travel with the text when it's copied and pasted elsewhere," but Anthropic doesn't really go into the technicalities of how this will work. For files such as images, Anthropic will use the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA) open standard . title: New surveillance tech links your phone to your license plate
author: Nicole M. Bennett, The Conversation
body: Imagine that you share a ride to work with the same colleague most mornings. As it passes by a license plate reader, the camera records the car, which can be linked through vehicle records to its registered owner. Beside it, another sensor detects signals broadcast by devices traveling nearby, such as your phone and your colleague’s smartwatch. After enough trips, software may treat some of those devices as a recurring electronic signature associated with the vehicle. Weeks later, one of the same device signals appears alongside a different car connected to an investigation. The signal itself may not contain its owner’s name, but its previous association with a known vehicle gives investigators another clue they can use to work out who was carrying the device. SignalTrace , a system marketed by the security company Leonardo , is designed to work alongside automatic license plate readers. The company says it can recognize groups of consumer devices that regularly move together, then associate them with license plate records and time-stamped locations. The pattern can then be searched even when a police investigator does not know the plate number. Read full article Comments

title: New Pass-ta-key attack reveals all the things we didn't know about passkeys
author: Dan Goodin
body: Last week a researcher outlined what he said was a “novel attack surface” in passkeys, the new authentication paradigm that offers a more secure alternative over password-based methods. In fact, the attacks demonstrated in the post are neither novel nor unique to passkeys. This distinction is important because the research has generated confusion among end users and security professionals as they assess whether this new mechanism is truly safe to use. The attack is called Pass-ta-key—a blending of the word passkey with the phrase “pass the key” and a nod to a plate of pasta. Arie Olshtein, a researcher at security firm Palo Alto Networks, described in a post last week how Pass-ta-key could obtain all passkeys stored in the Google Password Manager app (GPM) for Windows when it’s running on a machine infected with malware. This came as a surprise to many people because they believed passkeys are stored exclusively in the trusted platform manager (TPM), the locked-down enclave in a hardened silicon chip that’s reserved for storing cryptographic keys and other highly sensitive information on Windows machines. If passkeys are stored in the TPM, then how was Pass-ta-key able to extract the entire set of passkeys stored by the app, they wanted to know. Read full article Comments

title: ChatGPT will let you book a table mid-chat
body: People are using ChatGPT to sell their homes , message Tinder matches , book flights , browse their medical records , write essays , fabricate receipts , argue with their partners , shop online , talk to their cars , and order their coffee , and now they can make restaurant reservations within the app. Announced on Monday, OpenAI's chatbot now does Yelp reservations and waitlists, meaning users in the U.S. and Canada can directly book a table while chatting with ChatGPT. Want more tech and digital culture news delivered to your inbox daily or sent straight to your device? Sign up for Mashable's Top Stories newsletter or get Mashable push alerts today. According to Yelp's blog post , the integration will cover restaurants using Yelp Guest Manager, the app's front-of-house reservation and waitlist system. Once guests have booked a spot through ChatGPT, any changes to the reservation must be made through the Yelp app (not the chat). It's an extension of Yelp's partnership with ChatGPT, launched in July , which lets the chatbot legally use Yelp reviews, ratings, photos, and local business details to make recommendations. Featured Video For You Is ChatGPT Changing the Way We Write? ChatGPT's competitors have similar restaurant booking integrations. Google's Gemini is able to find, book, and manage reservations for restaurants on OpenTable using Reserve with Google. Microsoft Copilot can also book tables in the app using OpenTable , but, like ChatGPT's Yelp plug-in, you can't manage or cancel the reservation through the chatbot (this must be done in the OpenTable app). title: Tesla shows first Cybercab with built-in Starlink. Elon Musk explains why it needs one.
body: Tesla 's Cybercabs now come with built-in Starlink connectivity. On Monday, the company's Robotaxi account on X shared photos of the first Cybercab with an integrated Starlink antenna. Check it out up close in the photo below. It fits nicely. But is it needed? Credit: Tesla Given that Starlink is best suited for remote areas where there's no 5G connectivity, and Cybercabs will almost certainly first start operating in dense urban areas , why do Tesla's autonomous taxis even need Starlink? Cybercabs have 5G chips built-in, and the Starlink antenna adds additional cost, weight, and complexity which doesn't appear necessary right now. Tesla CEO Elon Musk has the answer, and it's definitely, absolutely, certainly not so that Tesla can foot another bill to Musk-owned SpaceX . In a tweet , he referenced Cloudflare's assessment that "bot traffic will exceed human (internet) traffic by a factor of 1,000 within five years." This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. "And the only system that can support the insanely fast bandwidth growth needed by AI is Starlink," wrote Musk in a reply. Ever since SpaceX's monster IPO in June, there's been talk about SpaceX and Tesla merging into one giant corporation that covers transportation, energy, AI, chipmaking, and AI compute, both on Earth and in space. title: Rare Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt variant discovered, to auction this week
body: Almost 100 rare Nintendo cartridges have been discovered in a Wisconsin retro games store, with a handful of them to go up for auction this week. The individually wrapped Super Mario Bros ./ Duck Hunt NES cartridges appear to have come from a previously unknown run of the games, with collectors having been unaware of their existence until now. SEE ALSO: 'The Super Mario Galaxy Movie' review: Death is coming for us all The 97 Super Mario Bros./Duck Hunt cartridges belong to Kevin Braun, owner of retro games store OneStopWonders in Waukesha, Wisconsin, and were identified with the help of Nintendo Wire editor Jason Ganos. Nintendo Wire reports that the cartridges were initially in the possession of a precious metal recovery service, which Nintendo appeared to have contracted to break them down. They were left untouched for decades, until Braun purchased the box of games from the owner's grandson. He had been intending to sell the games at OneStopWonders, but forgot them in a storage unit until they came up in conversation with Ganos. "After Kevin finished his story, I immediately could tell that the blood had drained from my face," Ganos wrote, recounting the discovery on Nintendo Wire. Super Mario Bros. and Duck Hunt aren't rare games in and of themselves. Released in the U.S. alongside the NES' 1985 launch, Super Mario Bros. and Duck Hunt have left enduring legacies as two of the platform's most popular titles. In 1988, the games were put together in dual cartridges and sold with the NES in an Action Set bundle. However, Braun's cartridges do not appear to be from this run.

title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on August 11
body: We're almost at the end of the Moon's current lunar cycle, with only the tiniest sliver surface still visible. That crescent will to shrink nothing over the next few nights before the Moon reaches its New Moon phase. What is today s Moon phase? As of Tuesday, Aug. 11, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon phase is in Waning Crescent phase, with 3% of its surface visible. The Moon is not illuminated enough to be able to spot anything on its surface tonight. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on August 28. What are Moon phases? The Moon doesn't look the same from Earth every night. As it travels around our planet, it moves through a lunar cycle that takes roughly 29.5 days to complete, according to NASA . The changing positions of the Sun, Earth, and Moon affect how much of the Moon's sunlit side we can see, creating the different phases. Over the course of the cycle, the Moon progresses from a narrow crescent to a half Moon and eventually a Full Moon, before starting the sequence over again. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it s not quite full yet. Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible. title: Trump signs bonkers order that cuts vaccines, promotes ones that don't exist
author: Beth Mole
body: President Trump signed an executive order Monday that makes sweeping, unilateral changes to federal vaccine recommendations. The order aims to reduce the number of lifesaving vaccines all children are recommended to get—from 18 to 11—while also splitting them up and spacing them out over more time and more medical visits. The vaccine changes are not backed by evidence or spurred by new findings. Rather, they are based on false anti-vaccine fearmongering about harms, including the debunked claim that they cause autism, and misinformation that multiple vaccinations can "overwhelm" children's immune systems. This false claim has also been repeatedly debunked and explained . During a signing event at the White House on Monday afternoon, Trump falsely claimed that pediatricians "have a vaccination that looks like the size of a bottle of soda," that is "poured into a little child's body, and bad things happen in too many cases. This is an explosion; this is an epidemic," Trump said. Read full article Comments

title: Amazon backs power plant that may become top source of US climate pollution
author: Ashley Belanger
body: Amazon’s artificial intelligence ambitions will soon be partly fueled by a natural gas-burning power plant in Texas that “could become the largest single source of climate pollution in the United States,” The New York Times reported . These gas-burning plants are increasingly lumped into data center projects. They produce harmful pollutants, which can accelerate climate change impacts and harm public health—contributing to conditions like asthma, heart disease, lung cancer, and strokes. Some communities are demanding more stringent environmental reviews, but the Trump administration favors fast-tracking that can include skipping the permitting process entirely. Since Elon Musk’s xAI controversially began relying on gas turbines last spring to power its biggest AI data center, Colossus, there has been public backlash to off-the-grid data centers like the one Amazon is building. title: Amazons robotaxi Zoox launches first paid service in U.S.
body: There s a new robotaxi in town Amazon's Zoox . Paid rides on Zoox became available for the first time ever, with service launching in Las Vegas on Monday (Aug. 10). The Sin City service follows Zoox's recent availability as a free option for select San Francisco riders. While Alphabet's autonomous Waymo cars are also available in Vegas , Zoox has some distinct differences, most notably its carriage-style seating made possible by the absence of a steering wheel and gas pedal. Zoox vehicles also lack a formal front or rear, allowing them to drive in either direction seamlessly. Riders adjust temperature and music choices on screens in the cabin. On July 30, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration announced that Zoox could temporarily offer paid service . "This temporary exemption will allow the commercial deployment of up to 2,500 vehicles annually for two years, subject to an enhanced, adaptable oversight structure that can evolve as Zoox s technology advances," according to the agency. Zoox prices will be competitive with other rideshare services, according to the Los Angeles Times , with possible surcharges for trips to airports or special events. The Zoox app shows rides currently available in a wide swath of the Las Vegas Valley, with vehicles operating from 11 a.m. to 1 a.m. On-demand service in Austin, Miami, and San Francisco will be up next. Waymo recently announced its van-style Ojai service is available for free to select riders in Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Phoenix. body: Games look gorgeous on its 7.9-inch screen. | Photo: Brandt Ranj / The Verge The cost of the Nintendo Switch 2 is going up by $50 on September 1st, 2026 , resulting in a $499.99 price tag for just the console. We’re just weeks away, but Costco is offering a fantastic $499.99 bundle for its members that includes a Nintendo Switch 2 , a 256GB microSD Express card ( usually $59 ), and a one year subscription to Nintendo Switch Online’s Expansion Pack tier, which normally costs $49.99 per year . That’s over $100 in value, and a great way to kickstart your Switch 2 experience. Nintendo Switch 2 Where to Buy: $558.98 $499.99 at Costco (with NSO and 256GB memory card) The Switch 2 has 256GB of internal storage, so a microSD card is likely something you’ll need eventually for storing more games without having to constantly manage your library. With first-party Nintendo games typically running between 10 and 25GB, and larger third-party games reaching 50GB, a 256GB card should store anywhere from 5-20 additional games. The Switch Online subscription includes a variety of features like cloud saving, online play, plus classic NES, SNES, and Game Boy titles. The Expansion Pack adds games from the GameCube, Game Boy Advance, N64, and Virtual Boy, and includes features for modern games, notably the Switch 2 upgrade packs for The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom. title: Supergirls Milly Alcock and Jason Momoa weigh in why nice isnt all that super
body: Supergirl is flying into theaters, and DC fans have plenty of reason to rejoice. The spinoff from 2025's Superman follows Kara (Milly Alcock), Clark Kent's cousin from Krypton, as she pub-crawls across the cosmos. Her plans for devil-may-care merriment are disrupted, however, when she crosses paths with an orphaned girl named Ruthye (Eve Ridley) on a quest for vengeance. Whether Supergirl likes it or not, she can't help but be the hero and the role model Ruthye needs. And along the way, she'll run into fiends and foes, including the outrageous bounty hunter Lobo ( Jason Momoa ). But above all, she offers a lesson that seems to fly in the face of her chipper cousin: Don't be nice. Be kind. When Entertainment Editor Kristy Puchko sat down in virtual interviews with Alcock, Momoa, and Supergirl screenwriter Ana Nogueira, they dug into what exactly that means. What's so bad about being nice? And what distinguishes being kind and being nice? And where does Lobo fit into this? You better believe Momoa and company had thoughts. Supergirl opens in theaters on June 26.

body: New Orleans, home to more than 300,000 residents and an emergency system that handles thousands of calls each day, is turning to AI for help. The city recently confirmed that emergency services, overseen by the Orleans Parish Communication District, are deploying an AI triage tool to screen and sort incoming calls to assist human operators. City representatives explained the technology is intended to reduce the number of repetitive calls and prevent lines from bottlenecking. Basically, if a resident calls in an incident that's already been reported, like a car crash, the AI dispatcher is supposed to handle it. SEE ALSO: AI companies keep destroying old books. Here's why. The tool, referred to as AI Emergency Call Triage, was developed by AI emergency services company Carbyne. It's still undergoing real-world testing by operators, according to reporting by the Shreveport Times, but has been involved in triaging traffic-related emergency calls since at least 2023 . The city also introduced an AI tool for its 311 non-emergency services in April. New Orleans is one of several cities introducing AI into emergency and non-emergency call operations, and Carbyne is already working with public safety agencies across the country. title: YouTube just raised the bar for creators to earn ad revenue
body: YouTube built one of the creator economy 's biggest payment systems, but now it is raising the bar for who gets to share in it. Beginning Feb. 1, 2027, new creators will need 8,000 qualified watch hours over the previous year or 20 million qualified Shorts views within 90 days to earn advertising and YouTube Premium revenue, the company announced Aug. 10 . This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. Both figures are double YouTube's current requirements of 4,000 watch hours or 10 million Shorts views. The announcement did not mention a change to the existing requirement that creators have at least 1,000 subscribers. The new rules will also affect creators who are already part of the YouTube Partner Program. To earn ad and subscription revenue from Shorts each month, they will need to maintain 10 million qualified views during a rolling 90-day period. Channels that fall below the threshold will remain in the program and can continue making money from long-form videos. Shorts revenue sharing will resume automatically if their views climb back above it. YouTube said creators who already earn "significant revenue" from Shorts are unlikely to be affected, but did not disclose how many channels currently fall short of the requirement. The updates mark the first significant overhaul of the Partner Program since 2018. Those newly supported handhelds include MSI's Claw 8 EX AI+, the extremely expensive , extremely powerful handheld built around Intel's Arc G3 processor that launched this summer. title: Spotify is testing a skip button that might let you skip podcast ads
body: Spotify has rolled out a feature that lets some users skip past podcast ads not sold directly by the platform, per an exclusive report from Semafor . In the report, Spotify frames the change as a streamlined version of its existing skip button, but publishers say it could gut their ad revenue. According to Semafor, Podnews called the update a "significant threat" to ad-funded shows, while Crooked Media co-founder Tommy Vietor was more direct, writing on social media that it was "very cool" of Spotify to "try and destroy the podcast industry." SEE ALSO: Spotify hits 300 million Premium subscribers Semafor reported that several major audio networks contacted Spotify directly after the announcement to raise concerns about their monetization. Privately, the company has argued that the feature actually helps publishers by keeping people listening longer overall, citing internal engagement data, while also stressing that the button is still in early testing and could be pulled back. A Spotify spokesperson confirmed to Semafor that the rollout is limited to certain paid subscribers and only appears when the app is open in the foreground, describing it as part of routine product testing aimed at making podcast listening "more intuitive" for Premium users. The move lands as the podcast industry is already contending with a broader shift toward video platforms like YouTube, Semafor noted, and it isn't the first time Spotify has drawn pushback from publishers the company partially reversed a podcast play-count rollout last year after similar complaints.

title: Following Epic loss, Google has started hosting rival app stores in the Play Store
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: A new day has dawned in the Play Store, and it's one that Google tried very hard to avoid. The first third-party app store has arrived in Google Play as a result of the long-running antitrust lawsuit with Epic . Those in the US can now head into Google Play and download Aptoide , a game-focused store that has been available as a sideloaded client since the early days of Android. Forcing Google to distribute third-party app stores in Google Play was one of several remedies imposed by Judge James Donato after Epic emerged victorious in 2023. The remedies also included lowering developer fees, mirroring Google Play apps in other app stores, and allowing developers to use alternative payment systems. But it was the app store stipulation that seemed to irk Google the most. Google almost avoided this outcome when it agreed to a settlement with Epic , which was announced early this year. Under the terms, Google would certify third-party app stores to allow users to install and use them with less friction, but it would not host them in Google Play. However, Google and Epic withdrew the settlement when it appeared the court would not approve it. This Registered App Store program is still slated to launch internationally, but in the US, Google is only doing what it must to comply with the judge's orders. Read full article Comments

title: Metas Muse Glimmer wants to bring AI agents to your laptop
body: Meta thinks the next front in the AI race may be sitting on your desk. On Aug. 10, Meta released Muse Glimmer , a 30-billion-parameter AI model designed to run locally on a Mac or PC with a single consumer GPU. Its weights are available to download from Hugging Face under a permissive Apache 2.0 license, allowing developers to use, modify, and build products with the model for free. That means Muse Glimmer can operate without sending every request to a distant data center. It can also work without an internet connection, provided the computer running it has enough memory and processing power. For anyone ready to open an app and start chatting, however, there is a catch: Muse Glimmer is a developer release. Meta is supplying the model that can power an AI agent, rather than a consumer product that immediately manages your inbox or reorganizes your desktop. What can Muse Glimmer actually do? Meta built Muse Glimmer for "agentic" work, meaning it can take a goal, divide it into steps, and use connected tools to complete parts of the task. The company imagines local agents that could manage schedules, draft messages, organize files, and write or debug code. The model can process images alongside text, perform multi-step tasks, and attempt recovery when a tool fails. Meta says it was trained on data from more than 100 languages. Fitting those abilities onto one computer required some downsizing. At full precision, Muse Glimmer would need more than 55 GB of memory. Meta compressed the model to below 20 GB, leaving additional room for its working memory and image-processing system

title: Dogs can tell if you're scared or sad
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: Any dog owner would tell you that their canine companions are attuned to their humans' emotional state and respond accordingly. Scientists have performed fMRI scans on dogs and identified a specific brain region that processes happy human facial expresses, like a smile, according to a new paper published in the journal iScience. They also found that dogs can tell the difference between negative facial expressions, specifically anger, sadness, and fear. “Humans are really good at picking up small details on the face, and so are dogs,” said co-author Raúl Hernández-Pérez of the University of Vienna. “This makes dogs very interesting. By studying their brains, we can understand what adaptations have developed to support their remarkable social and emotional understanding of humans.” Prior behavioral studies have shown that dogs are sensitive to emotion in human faces. Dogs will, for example, choose a box their human has identified with a happy expression over one the human treats with fear or disgust. Past fMRI studies found that an area in the canine left temporal cortex showed a stronger response to human faces compared to dog faces, as well as a greater response in the caudate, hippocampus, and amygdala to human faces showing emotion versus neutral faces. Raise it a few inches, wrap the lower body in plastic cladding, name it for the Australian bush, and suburban families would drive to soccer practice while imagining themselves fording streams and climbing sand dunes. In giving birth to the Legacy Outback in 1995, Subaru more or less created the template for the modern, adventure-minded, off-road-themed crossover. By the 2000 model year, the Outback had graduated from trim level to standalone model, and it has been paying the bulk of Subaru's bills ever since. Today, the 2026 Outback marks a new era in the model's history. The wagon silhouette that defined six generations has given way to a sharpened two-box shape that's much more at home parked next to an upright Forester or Ascent. title: A researcher bought noreply.net. Companies started sending him secrets.
author: Matt Burgess, wired.com
body: Cory Solovewicz receives more unwanted emails than you. Seriously—it’s a lot more. Since December 2024, one of the domains at which the security researcher receives email has registered 401,796 messages—by his calculations that’s an average of 699.99 pings per day. This deluge isn’t the regular flood of spam, newsletters, and unwanted deals that fill many people’s inboxes. Instead, companies and other organizations are inadvertently sending Solovewicz other people’s private information and company secrets. Over the last few years, he’s received injury reports from a city government, confirmation of people’s pizza orders, and account setup emails from a school platform. “I get service orders for people that need repairs. I get lots of test platform credentials,” says Solovewicz , a security researcher and consultant. Solovewicz is receiving the avalanche of messages as he’s the owner of the domains noreply.us and noreply.net , which he purchased in 2020 and 2024, respectively. After originally planning to use the noreply.us domain as a catch-all email—which receives mail sent to any @ address on that domain—to filter messages and enhance his privacy, the researcher quickly noticed that other systems were sending mail to @ noreply.us addresses. “I created an accidental honeypot,” Solovewicz tells WIRED. “I had no idea it was going to turn into this.” Read full article Comments

title: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 survives the ultimate stress test
body: Foldable phones have been around for a while, but I still regularly get people asking me whether they're going to break in half. On Sunday, YouTuber JerryRigEverything tried to do just that to Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 ...and couldn't. SEE ALSO: Review: The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 makes phones interesting again JerryRigEverything put Samsung's foldable through his typically rough set of tests to see how it'll hold up. This included scratching the display with a utility knife and burning it with a lighter. The damage was there, of course, but it wasn't fatal. Then, JerryRigEverything tried the ultimate test by bending the phone in the direction opposite of its folding mechanism. Again, there was significant damage to the phone's hinge, and this is something that you should never do to your phone. At the end of it, however, the phone was still alive and kicking, and there was barely any damage to its display. Being limited to one device only, the test obviously isn't perfect, but it's a testament to how far Samsung has progressed in building its foldable phones to last. As a reminder, check out what the same YouTuber's tests did to the original Samsung Galaxy Fold a few years back .

body: American filmmaker Jane Schoenbrun loves fucked-up horror stories. In 2021, they broke through with We're All Going to the World's Fair , a gnarly coming-of-age story with a creepypasta vibe. Three years later, Schoenbrun delivered the critically heralded I Saw the TV Glow , which used a fictional Buffy the Vampire Slayer -like series to explore emerging trans identity. Now, with Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma , Schoenbrun offers a tale of queer joy in the mold of a slasher comedy. SEE ALSO: 'Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma' review: Laughing in the face of 'elevated horror' Hacks ' Hannah Einbinder stars as Kris, a queer indie filmmaker entrusted with resurrection the "zombie IP" that is Camp Miasma. The iconic slasher film begat eight increasingly deranged sequels and immortalized its Southern-fried Final Girl, played by Billy Presley (Gillian Anderson). To get the reboot right, Kris travels to the abandoned summer camp where the first movie was shot so she can meet Presley, who's now an eccentric recluse. Together, they talk fried chicken, desire, and Little Death (Jack Haven), the slasher who rises from the lake to wreak havoc on Camp Miasma counselors. To dive into the depths of Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma, Schoenbrun and Einbinder visited Mashable's Say More studio to speak with Entertainment Editor Kristy Puchko. Together, they explored the inspiration points for this surreal and silly slasher, celebrated the return of horny movies, and (naturally!) compared gummies and talked Counting Crows. The company, which created the world's first modular exoskeleton, has launched its H Series, now available for purchase: the H Pro and the H Ultra . The H Pro is the lighter, more everyday option, built for walking, fitness, and lighter outdoor activity, with up to 25 kilometers of assisted range. title: Peer review is overwhelmed—can it survive in the AI era?
author: Saima Sidik
body: Jason Semprini was excited about his research on policies mandating that elementary school students receive the human papillomavirus vaccine. HPV causes most cases of cervical cancer, but counterintuitively, Semprini found that mandates don’t do that much to reduce the overall rate of cervical cancer in a population. That’s odd, but it's also not completely surprising—we know that mandating a vaccine can motivate some people to find ways to avoid it. Semprini wrote up the study and submitted the manuscript to a journal, where it was sent out for peer review, a long-standing process through which other researchers in the field assess the validity of research and make a recommendation on whether or not it should be published. This is usually done anonymously and on a volunteer basis. In this case, the reviewer did not share Semprini’s excitement. That may have stemmed from a misunderstanding of the study’s central message: The reviewer mistakenly thought Semprini was questioning whether the HPV vaccine itself prevents cervical cancer rather than studying the effectiveness of a policy meant to increase vaccination rates. “There’s a very big difference there,” said Semprini, who is a health economist at Des Moines University. title: A major Apple Watch redesign may be coming
body: Apple is considering a major overhaul of its Apple Watch, though what exactly that means is still very uncertain. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says that the company's next Apple Watch versions that are coming out this year will only get "modest upgrades," which includes a performance boost, new colors and bands, health and fitness upgrades, and possibly a ceramic case variant, though it's unclear whether that'll happen this or next year. In the future, however, bigger changes are in the works. According to Gurman, Apple is looking into wearables of all sorts, including ones with no displays, and those with different types of screens and various sizes. Yes, that's pretty vague, but when you consider that Apple Watch has pretty much looked the same since day one, it would be a pretty big move by Apple. Apple is also reportedly considering premium models "beyond the Ultra and Herm s variants," as well as cheaper models than the Apple Watch SE. It's early days, and Gurman says the company hasn't settled on a single direction yet, and that the changes will "take time." SEE ALSO: The latest iPhone 18 news, leaks, and rumors: Release date, price increases, and color options Gurman also touched on the iPhone, saying that Apple is already planning a second and a third version of its upcoming foldable iPhone, scheduled to arrive in 2027 and 2028, respectively. Those variants will have "slightly larger displays," both on the inside and the outside.

title: The solar eclipse is this week — but dont take photos of it with your phone
body: I learned that my iPhone 15 Pro Max and the upcoming 2026 total solar eclipse do not mix. I stumbled upon BGR' s article, which warned skygazers against using their phones to take pictures of the imminent cosmic event. If you're like me, you may be wondering "Why?" After all, who wouldn't want to snap a photo of such an awe-inspiring celestial occurrence? As it turns out, taking a photo of the 2026 solar eclipse could damage your iPhone's camera hardware. SEE ALSO: Solar eclipse 2026 from the US: how to watch from home and online Why you shouldn't take a photo of the 2026 solar eclipse with your phone In the same way that you shouldn't use a telescope or binoculars to gaze at the sun (you could melt your eyeballs off), you shouldn't use your phone's shooter or any other poorly equipped camera to take a photo of the solar eclipse. BGR says that no smartphone is designed to handle the intense solar rays the sun emanates. "Using your camera or phone could cause the heat from the rays to become so concentrated that it could melt the lens inside," the tech outlet warned. Days before the April 8, 2024 eclipse that swept across parts of North America, NASA provided similar advice. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. There is a workaround in that you can purchase filters for your phone and camera . NEEWER 67mm Clip On Filters Kit for Phone Camera Credit: Amazon But the best way to see the eclipse might very well be with your eyes rather than a camera lens. That is, if they are fully protected. title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on August 10
body: If you thought the Moon looked small last night, it'll be even thinner this evening as it continues to wane ahead of the New Moon in a few night's time. What is today s Moon phase? As of Monday, Aug. 10, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon phase is in Waning Crescent phase, with 16% of its surface visible. To see anything on the Moon's surface tonight, you'll need either binoculars or a telescope. With these, you'll be able to see the Grimaldi Basin , a huge ancient crater on the Moon, formed by a massive asteroid collision. Its center was later flooded with dark basalt rock, creating the distinctive shadowy area surrounded by a brighter rim. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on August 28. What are Moon phases? The Moon's appearance changes throughout the month as it orbits Earth, completing one full lunar cycle approximately every 29.5 days, according to NASA . During that journey, the positions of the Sun, Earth, and Moon are constantly shifting, altering how much of the Moon's illuminated surface is visible from our perspective. That's why we see the familiar sequence of phases, from a slim crescent to a half Moon, then a Full Moon, before the pattern begins again. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. title: House of the Dragon Season 3: How does the Battle of Tumbleton compare to the book?
body: Ever since Ormund Hightower (James Norton) took over the town of Tumbleton in House of the Dragon Season 3, episode 3, fans knew the Battle of Tumbleton was imminent. SEE ALSO: 'House of the Dragon' gives Alys Rivers a tragic backstory that isn't in the book One of the most infamous battles in George R.R. Martin's Fire and Blood , the Battle of Tumbleton is a resounding defeat for Rhaenyra's forces, made all the worse by the betrayal of some of her dragonriders. House of the Dragon 's Season 3 finale gets these broad strokes right, but just like with the Battle of the Gullet , several key details are different from the source material. From missing traitors to new participants, here are the biggest differences between House of the Dragon 's Battle of Tumbleton and Fire and Blood 's. House of the Dragon reverses who's laying siege to who in the Battle of Tumbleton. Tommy Flanagan in "House of the Dragon." Credit: Theo Whiteman / HBO When the Battle of Tumbleton breaks out in Fire and Blood , Rhaenyra's forces hold the town, while Ormund's armies attack. House of the Dragon reverses this. By the time the battle happens, Ormund has a long-established presence in Tumbleton, and it's Rhaenyra who's had to weigh whether to attack or not. SEE ALSO: When is 'House of the Dragon' Season 4 coming out? The switcheroo offers up several opportunities for House of the Dragon . On one side of the war, it amplifies Rhaenyra's moral dilemma: Should she attack Tumbleton and risk harming her subjects, or should she take a peaceful approach and be labeled as weak? body: Corlys Velaryon (Steve Toussaint) is a legendary warrior and a key player in Rhaenyra Targaryen's (Emma D'Arcy) war efforts. But in House of the Dragon 's Season 3 finale, the formidable Sea Snake is all about peace. We start the season by seeing Corlys in full battle mode at the Battle of the Gullet, but by the end of the season, he's trying his best to sue for peace. Walk me through the way he's changed and the way his thoughts on the war have changed from the Battle of the Gullet to the Battle of Tumbleton. Steve Toussaint: I think that arc began even before this season, towards the end of Season 2. In fact, it could be argued that it started even before that. title: House of the Dragon Season 3 foreshadowed its saddest finale moment
body: House of the Dragon foreshadows character fates aplenty throughout the series, and the Season 3 finale is no exception. In the final episode, the death of Helaena (Phia Saban) is a tragic, devastating moment, with the princess leaving behind an embroidered tapestry of prophecies for Queen Rhaenyra (Emma D'Arcy) to reflect on. Elsewhere, Helaena's mother, Alicent (Olivia Cooke) , is in a camp in the woods, having fled from Harrenhal. Her expression shows she's aware something is wrong, as the queen dowager considers a butterfly, then two, then hundreds rising up into the sky. This sombre moment in House of the Dragon sees a mother connected with her fallen daughter, without having to deliver the news. And these beautiful butterflies were foreshadowed earlier in the season in scenes that make it even more shattering. SEE ALSO: 'House of the Dragon' Season 3 family tree: How Targaryens, Hightowers, and Velaryons connect In Season 3, episode 2, right before Rhaenyra takes King's Landing , then-Queen Helaena sits in a palace garden examining a caterpillar. "This is strange," she says to her mother. "It isn't the season." Alicent hastily closes her daughter's journal, but not before seeing Helaena's studious sketch of a butterfly within it. Credit: Ollie Upton / HBO It's not the only moment of foreshadowing, either. In Season 3, episode 5, Helaena and Alicent are now captives in the Red Keep, under Rhaenyra's orders. title: House of the Dragon Season 3 finale: Is Daeron Targaryen dead?
body: House of the Dragon 's Season 3 finale knocked several key characters off the board, including Lord Ormund Hightower (James Norton). (Rest in peace, you odor-hating icon.) However, one Team Green member's fate is still up in the air: What's happened to Prince Daeron Targaryen (Benjamin Evan Ainsworth)? SEE ALSO: 'House of the Dragon' gives Alys Rivers a tragic backstory that isn't in the book Ormund's reluctant king-to-be was last seen fleeing through the burning streets of Tumbleton with his uncle, Gwayne Hightower (Freddie Fox). However, in the battle's aftermath, Gwayne finds himself alone in the rubble, calling out for Daeron. Could the prince still be alive, or did he join Ormund in death? House of the Dragon has always played by the rule that if you haven't seen a corpse, the character isn't dead yet. Take this season's multiple Corlys Velaryon (Steve Toussaint) fake-outs , or the return of Tyland Lannister (Jefferson Hall) . Just like with them, we haven't seen Daeron's dead body, so we can assume he's likely survived the Battle of Tumbleton. Notably, House of the Dragon also hasn't revealed the fate of his dragon, Tessarion. Could he have escaped on dragonback and chosen to regroup? What happens to Daeron in Fire and Blood ? While House of the Dragon does differ substantially from its source material, George R.R. Martin's Fire and Blood , we can still look to the book for a blueprint of what's next for Daeron. body: Burning bridges with the most connected person in King's Landing could have consequences for Queen Rhaenyra ( Emma D'Arcy ). In the House of the Dragon Season 3 finale, the Westeros monarch makes a sudden decision to dismiss her Mistress of Whispers, Mysaria (Sonoya Mizuno). Even lady's maid Elinda (Jordon Stevens) seems shocked to the deliver the news, as guards pack up Mysaria's things. But why does Rhaenyra make such an abrupt move to spurn her lover and confidante, an OG of her Small Council , and the most informed person in the capital? Season 2 saw Rhaenyra (Emma D'Arcy) and Mysaria (Sonoya Mizuno) inseparable. Without getting into the King's Landing HR weeds (Westeros' rulers would all be jailed if we went down this road), this is a clear abuse of power on Rhaenyra's part. body: Ulf the White (Tom Bennett) starts and ends House of the Dragon Season 3 the way he means to go on: taking a crap whenever he bloody well likes. The turncoat dragonseed began his journey this season joining the illustrious Westeros tradition of pooping on camera , and in the final episode, he's once again found on the bog in the middle of the action. Searching high and low for Ulf around Tumbleton, soldiers finally locate the man, whom we last saw drinking himself into a stupor on the eve of battle and trash-talking Team Black. Passed out on the toilet, Ulf is dragged pants-down out onto the street by his new boss, Ormund Hightower (James Norton), and given a what-for that deeply pisses him off. It's all-too-familiar treatment that makes Ulf furious, deciding he's no one's errand boy not Ormund's nor Daemon's (Matt Smith). He's a dragonrider, one of the rarest roles in Westeros, and he and Silverwing dracarys their way through both armies. "You know what? That did go through my head. title: House of the Dragon Season 3 finale: Helaenas tapestry, explained
body: There are many tragic story arcs in House of the Dragon , but perhaps none more so than that of Helaena (Phia Saban). The princess has been in a downward spiral in Season 3 , held prisoner in King's Landing by Rhaenyra ( Emma D'Arcy ) with less and less access to the outdoors and basically no family left . Not idly spending her time imprisoned in King's Landing, she was, in fact, weaving a lengthy, detailed tapestry. But given we already know Helaena has the ability to see glimpses of the future , what clues might be hiding in it? SEE ALSO: 'House of the Dragon' Season 3 family tree: How Targaryens, Hightowers, and Velaryons connect What happens to Helaena in the Season 3 finale? Things go from bad to worse. Passing recently-sacked Mistress of Whispers Lady Mysaria (Sonoya Mizuno) in the courtyard, Helaena learns that her brother-husband Aegon (Tom Glynn-Carney) is still alive . "Your unborn child is a hostage," hisses Mysaria. "She will never release you." Earlier in the season, we (and Rhaenyra) learned that Helaena is pregnant with Aegon's child, a boy and another direct threat to Rhaenyra's claim to the throne. Following a tense exchange with Rhaenyra in the season finale about the "ugliness" of the queen's rule and her refusal to eat, Helaena is restrained by the guards and force fed. At the end of the episode, with her tapestry finally finished, Helaena walks towards her room's open window. title: House of the Dragon gives Alys Rivers a tragic backstory that isnt in the book
body: For two seasons now, Alys Rivers (Gayle Rankin) has been House of the Dragon 's most mysterious ensemble character. As the de facto keeper of Harrenhal, she's guided troubled Targaryen men through vision quests , guarded dragon eggs , and even proclaimed herself to be a witch. Through it all, her own history has remained largely nebulous. Yes, she wants Harrenhal, as well as dragons to protect it. But why? Why is she so attached to this wretched stronghold? House of the Dragon 's Season 3 finale lays it all bare, revealing a tragic backstory for Alys that is nowhere to be found in George R.R. Martin's Fire and Blood . SEE ALSO: 'House of the Dragon' Season 3 family tree: How Targaryens, Hightowers, and Velaryons connect What is Alys Rivers' backstory? In a vulnerable scene with Aemond Targaryen (Ewan Mitchell), Alys tells him a story that dates all the way back to the time of Aegon the Conqueror. During his conquest of Westeros, Aegon faced opposition from the tyrannical Harren Hoare, King of the Isles and the Rivers. Also known as Harren the Black, he holed himself up in his castle of Harrenhal, believing he could withstand any attacks from Aegon. However, he didn't account for dragonfire, which he realized too late when Aegon's dragon Balerion the Black Dread laid waste to Harrenhal, barbecuing Harren and his sons inside. The burning of Harrenhal is thought to mark the end of Harren's line, but as Alys tells Aemond, one boy survived. He was badly burned, and his mother did everything she could to save him. title: When is House of the Dragon Season 4 coming out?
body: The dust is still settling after the Battle of Tumbleton in House of the Dragon 's Season 3 finale, and if you're anything like me, you're wondering, When are we going to see what happens next? SEE ALSO: 'House of the Dragon' Season 3 family tree: How Targaryens, Hightowers, and Velaryons connect The good news is that House of the Dragon Season 4 is already on the way. HBO announced the Season 4 renewal in Nov. 2025, along with a Season 2 renewal for the yet-unreleased A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms . As part of that announcement, HBO confirmed it had plans to release these seasons through 2028. A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms Season 2 will come first, in 2027, while House of the Dragon Season 4 is slated for 2028. The exact release date for House of the Dragon Season 4 has yet to be announced, as Season 4 hasn't even started filming. However, given that every season of House of the Dragon has premiered in the summer (Season 1 in August, Seasons 2 and 3 in June), it's highly likely Season 4 will follow this trend and continue being HBO's summer tentpole release. So get ready for yet another two-year wait between seasons, an unfortunate norm in today's streaming age. (Remember when the wait between Game of Thrones seasons was just a year?) Is House of the Dragon Season 4 the show's final season? However, this two-year wait for more House of the Dragon may be the last one fans will have to endure, as it's highly likely that Season 4 will be the show's last. title: NYT Pips hints, answers for August 10, 2026
body: Welcome to your guide to Pips, the latest game in the New York Times catalogue. Released in August 2025, Pips puts a unique spin on dominoes, creating a fun single-player experience that could become your next daily gaming habit. Currently, if you're stuck, the game only offers to reveal the entire puzzle, forcing you to move on to the next difficulty level and start over. However, we have you covered! Below are piecemeal answers that will serve as hints so that you can find your way through each difficulty level. How to play Pips If you've ever played dominoes, you'll have a passing familiarity with how Pips is played. As we've shared in our previous hints stories for Pips, the tiles, like dominoes, are placed vertically or horizontally and connect with each other. The main difference between a traditional game of dominoes and Pips is the color-coded conditions you have to address. The touching tiles don't necessarily have to match. body: Everything is becoming more expensive, including things that are supposed to be cheap. The latest example is DeepSeek's AI services, as reported by Bloomberg . The Chinese AI firm sent a notice to users on Thursday warning of a "significant" price increase, though it did not specify just how significant it would be. DeepSeek has been known for its extremely cheap services relative to the competition, especially with regards to its western counterparts, so this is probably not the most welcome news among DeepSeek users. SEE ALSO: DeepSeek reportedly won't be banned in U.S. (for now) To be more specific, DeepSeek currently charges less than a dollar per million input and output tokens, which is how AI services are sold to customers. By comparison, Anthropic's Fable 5 model charges $10 per million input and $50 per million output tokens. It was probably unsustainable for DeepSeek to continue charging so little compared to the competition, especially as the company plans to build a huge data center in Inner Mongolia. But still, you can't count on anything staying cheap anymore. Not even AI, the thing that's making everything else expensive in the first place.

title: Amazons new Texas AI data center will include massive amounts of air pollution
body: In 2019, Amazon signed the Climate Pledge , aiming to help Earth's environmental health. In 2026, Amazon aims to set a record for the most air pollution emitted by a single power plant. The New York Times reported that the company is building a new natural-gas-burning power plant in Pecos County, Texas, for a huge AI data center project. The plant, if built as planned, would emit approximately 33 million tons of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere annually, making it among the largest emitters in the United States. SEE ALSO: Texas, yes Texas, puts limits on data centers AI data centers are already known to have multiple huge downsides to their construction. Aside from their huge carbon emissions , they're also known for generating massive amounts of noise pollution , and they can raise utility bills for nearby residents if they use the local electrical grid. Amazon's new plant won't necessarily do the last thing, as it's providing its own power using natural gas, but the proposed carbon emissions would still be damaging to the environment. Construction of the plant appears to be proceeding despite recent pushback from the Texas government on data centers. As for Amazon's Climate Pledge, a spokesperson told the NYT that, simply put, things change over time. "The world looks different now than when we co-founded the climate pledge," the spokesperson told the New York Times .

title: Mount Toba eruption doesn't seem like it could nearly kill our species
author: Jacek Krywko
body: Mount Toba was the biggest volcanic eruption in the last 2.6 million years, and some have suggested it nearly wiped out humanity. Around 74,000 years ago, a caldera on what is now Sumatra emptied thousands of cubic kilometers of magma in about two weeks, roughly a thousand times more than Mount Pinatubo spewed out in 1991. “People thought it might have caused massive cooling of the planet, and hence threatened the survival of our ancestors,” says Jinheum Park, a geoscientist at Johannes Gutenberg University in Mainz, Germany. Park and his colleagues went looking for the records of that catastrophe in the mud taken from the bottom of a small crater lake on the Kenya-Tanzania border. They found instead that the effects of the Mount Toba eruption lasted under two years and amounted to perhaps half a degree of cooling. Muddy calendars Volcanic eruptions inject sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere, where it becomes a haze of tiny droplets that reflect sunlight back into space. Bigger eruptions eject more sulfur dioxide and, in principle, cause more cooling. But this trend stops working when the eruption exceeds a certain magnitude. “Bigger sulfate aerosols settle quickly, because they are heavier,” Park explains. This quick settling makes them less effective in scattering incoming solar radiation. Read full article Comments

title: I found 1 major reason to shell out $650 for the Sony 1000X the Collexion headphones
body: When I started reviewing Sony's most expensive consumer headphones yet, I naturally expected them to offer an elevated experience. I didn't expect to hear the best spatial audio I've ever encountered. I say this, too, as someone who has been left completely unimpressed by spatial audio features time and time again. Be forewarned, though: the Sony 1000X the Collexion headphones clock in at a whopping $649.99 putting them nearly $200 higher than the WH-1000XM6 . The reason for the fanfare? The Collexions are the 10th anniversary celebration of the 1000X line (hence the...creative name). The brand certainly delivers on some of its best features in the Collexion headphones, but really, the experience for the high price point is only likely to appeal to a select few who prioritize sound and looks above all else. The Sony 1000X the Collexion at a glance These aren't the 1000X headphones you're used to. Credit: Bethany Allard / Mashable What I liked: These are the best sounding headphones Sony's made, and the spatial audio with the 360 Upmix tech really highlights that. The lack of hard plastic usually found on Sony's headphones makes the look more sleek and luxe, and the wear feels plush and comfortable. The noise cancellation is still solid, too. title: Solar eclipse 2026 from the US: how to watch from home and online
body: If your feeds are blowing up with talk of the upcoming total solar eclipse , this might burst your bubble: The show might not be coming to a sky near you. On Aug. 12, the moon will sweep its shadow across the top of the world, briefly turning day into twilight along a narrow path through Greenland, Iceland, northern Russia, northern Spain, and a sliver of Portugal. That's the path of totality where the sun is completely blocked and it's the first time in 27 years that mainland Europe has gotten a full, real-deal solar eclipse. But people in the United States won't be in that bullseye. Instead, a part of the country will see a partial solar eclipse, where the moon nips the sun but never covers it completely. The sky won't go dark, the stars won't pop out, and you won't get the full moody effect . But with the right eyewear, you could still see the sun turn into a yummy space crescent roll in the middle of a Wednesday. For a U.S. audience, this eclipse is either a drop-everything-and-fly-to-Iceland kind of deal or a fun coffee break at work. Here's how to plan 15 minutes to step outside and look up safely or, better yet, ditch the special eyewear and get a front-row seat to the main event with a livestream from where the real action is happening. title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on August 9
body: The New Moon is only a few nights away, so there's less and less of the Moon to see each evening. Here's what it'll look like tonight. What is today s Moon phase? As of Sunday, Aug. 9, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon phase is in Waning Crescent phase, with 16% of its surface visible. Without visual aids, you'll only be able to see the Aristarchus Plateau. However, if you have binoculars or a telescope, you'll also see the Grimaldi Basin. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on August 28. What are Moon phases? The Moon's appearance changes throughout the month as it orbits Earth, completing one full lunar cycle approximately every 29.5 days, according to NASA . During that journey, the positions of the Sun, Earth, and Moon are constantly shifting, altering how much of the Moon's illuminated surface is visible from our perspective. That's why we see the familiar sequence of phases, from a slim crescent to a half Moon, then a Full Moon, before the pattern begins again. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it s not quite full yet. Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible. title: X retires revenue sharing for new Original Content Rewards program
body: X is overhauling how it pays creators, phasing out its long-running Revenue Sharing program in favor of a new system called the Original Content Rewards Program. The platform's Creators account announced the change in a post , saying the program is meant to "reward creators who bring original ideas, expertise, reporting, creativity, and commentary to X." According to the announcement, X stopped accepting new Revenue Sharing enrollments immediately and will wind the program down entirely after Sept. 7. Creators currently enrolled will receive three final payouts two on the standard schedule in mid- and late August, and a final payment around Sept. 11 covering earnings through the cutoff date. Starting Sept. 8, existing Revenue Sharing members can apply for the new program if they meet its eligibility requirements, the company said. SEE ALSO: With the launch of X Money, Elon Musk gets one step closer to his 'everything app' Per X's announcement, the new program ties earnings to "qualified impressions" a creator's original content receives, rather than the advertising-revenue split that defined the old system. Qualified impressions must come from unique, verified Premium subscribers viewing at least half of a post on the Home Timeline; impressions that are duplicated, paid, promoted, or fraudulent don't count. title: DeepMind’s hurricane breakthrough has surprised weather scientists
author: Victoria Turk, wired.com
body: In October 2025, a storm brewed over the Caribbean Sea. Weather models differed on its trajectory. Would it remain weak and end up in Haiti, or would it intensify and head to Jamaica? Artificial intelligence model WeatherNext, developed by Google’s DeepMind and Google Research, went with the latter. Five days before landfall, it predicted with 80 percent confidence that the storm system would hit Jamaica as a Category 5 hurricane. Hurricane Melissa was catastrophic, causing flooding and landslides across Jamaica. But the AI model helped forecasters give an earlier warning to communities in its path, so they could better prepare. In a paper published on Thursday in Nature, researchers show that the WeatherNext AI model can predict cyclones with unprecedented accuracy. On average, it gives forecasters a day more lead time than existing models; this means its predictions three days out are as accurate as previous models’ predictions two days out. On the ground, that extra day can mean a lot. Read full article Comments

title: Pluto has a heart. Scientists discovered that its bleeding.
body: Pluto 's famous heart is bleeding, according to new research, hinting that the distant world is more alive than it looks. That bright, heart-shaped glacier has been a fan favorite ever since NASA 's New Horizons spacecraft flew past the cold outer world in 2015. Scientists now say the heart isn't just the dwarf planet's special cutie mark , it may be slowly leaking liquid yes, liquid onto the surface. Researchers say dark streaks along the heart's rim are actually stains left by liquid nitrogen that recently seeped through cracks, flowed, and refroze. The new evidence makes a compelling case that Pluto isn't a frozen, dead world it may have working "plumbing" under its ice. "Pluto never stops surprising us," said Alan Stern, principal investigator of the New Horizons mission, in a statement . "In addition to suggesting that liquids have recently expressed themselves on Pluto's surface, it also suggests a new kind of time-variable feature on Pluto." SEE ALSO: One lucky orbiter caught the SpaceX rocket crash site on moon "Recently" here means roughly within the last million years, not last Tuesday. Still, by geological standards, that could mean this activity is ongoing today. Despite the fact that the New Horizons flyby happened a decade ago, scientists are still unpacking the enormous, once-in-a-generation dataset that came from it. Early work tackled some of the big-picture questions, like what is Pluto made of. title: AI companies keep destroying old books. Heres why.
body: The AI industry, not content with alienating top creators , seems to be intent on alienating book lovers too. That much is clear in the wake of a 404 Media report on ISBNdb , a company that tracks book data and briefly offered "AI training data" in the form of "the world's largest book database." So far so normal; AI companies looking to build better AI models are hungry for fresh data from any source that isn't the internet. Books generally better edited and more cogent than your average Reddit thread make AI sound smart. (There's a premium on books published before 2022, ironically because we can't be sure if books were written by AI after that date.) But on a now-deleted page, ISBNdb also advertised a "legally-binding nondisclosure agreement" that would hide an AI company client's "identity and strategy." Why? ISBNdb explained: "Destroying millions of books evokes images of burning libraries ... the optics problem is real. 'AI company destroys two million books' is not a headline that generates sympathy." Indeed. Turns out ISBNdb was offering destructive book scanning, an industrial process that claims to turn pages into data faster than the "move a page, take a picture" alternative by slicing the spines off books and feeding the pages into a scanning machine, photocopier style, then recycliny them. (ISBNdb's now-deleted advice: "lead with the recycling story, not the destruction story." But if you just recoiled with horror at the destruction story, you're not alone. title: What is OpenAI Astra? Everything we know about the quantum math-solving model.
body: Do you understand quantum parallel repetition? What about quantum complexity, lattice cryptography, or extremal combinatorics? The new OpenAI model Astra knows all about them. Recently, OpenAI confirmed the existence of Astra , calling it "our next major model." On Aug. 1, the ChatGPT-maker revealed that "an internal version of Astra" solved 10 major open math problems, some of which have been unresolved for decades. Then, on Aug. 7, OpenAI announced that Astra had developed such advanced cyber capabilities that new security controls were necessary and that some internal development work would be paused. "These results, in addition to expert assessments, have led us to conclude last night that we cannot rule out critical cyber capabilities under our Preparedness Framework ." OpenAI's Preparedness Framework is the company's "approach to tracking and preparing for frontier capabilities" that could be dangerous. It tracks risk levels in three categories: biological and chemical, cybersecurity, and AI self-improvement. Previously, GPT-5.6-Sol was evaluated as a "high" risk in cybersecurity, and so Astra could be the first OpenAI model to be classified as a "critical" risk. "Under our Preparedness Framework, a model reaches the Critical cybersecurity threshold if it can identify and develop functional zero-day exploits of all severity levels in many hardened real-world critical systems without human intervention, or can devise and execute end-to-end novel strategies for cyberattacks against hardened targets given only a high level desired goal," OpenAI's blog post states. title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on August 8
body: We're getting closer to the New Moon, so the Moon's visibility will drop significantly over the coming nights. Keep reading to find out what, if anything, you can spot tonight. What is today s Moon phase? As of Saturday, Aug. 8, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon phase is in Waning Crescent phase, with 26% of its surface visible. Without visual aids, you should be able to catch a glimpse of the Aristarchus Plateau and the Kepler Crater. Plus, binoculars or a telescope will help you to see the Grimaldi Basin, the Gassendi Crater, and the Mare Humorum. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on August 28. What are Moon phases? The Moon's appearance changes throughout the month as it orbits Earth, completing one full lunar cycle approximately every 29.5 days, according to NASA . During that journey, the positions of the Sun, Earth, and Moon are constantly shifting, altering how much of the Moon's illuminated surface is visible from our perspective. That's why we see the familiar sequence of phases, from a slim crescent to a half Moon, then a Full Moon, before the pattern begins again. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. body: Welcome to your guide to Pips, the latest game in the New York Times catalogue. Released in August 2025, Pips puts a unique spin on dominoes, creating a fun single-player experience that could become your next daily gaming habit. How to play Pips If you've ever played dominoes, you'll have a passing familiarity with how Pips is played. As we've shared in our previous hints stories for Pips, the tiles, like dominoes, are placed vertically or horizontally and connect with each other. The main difference between a traditional game of dominoes and Pips is the color-coded conditions you have to address. The touching tiles don't necessarily have to match. SEE ALSO: Wordle today: Answer, hints for August 8, 2026 The conditions you have to meet are specific to the color-coded spaces. For example, if it provides a single number, every side of a tile in that space must add up to the number provided. It is possible and common for only half a tile to be within a color-coded space. Here are common examples you'll run into across the difficulty levels: Number : All the pips in this space must add up to the number.
